newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY RULING PARTIES AGREE MINISTER APPOINTEES.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY RULING PARTIES AGREE MINISTER APPOINTEES.

text.p: Hungary's government said on Thursday two parties of the ruling coalition agreed about the appointees to replace Tamas Suchman, who was Industry and Trade Minister, also responsible for privatisation.
"There was no debate on the nomination Szabolcs Fazakas as industry and trade minister, " government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following the government's session.

The junior party of the coalition (SZDSZ) also acknowledged that Fazakas would not undertake supervising privatisation, and SZDSZ accepted the proposal to nominate Judit Csiha as privatisation minister, Kiss added.
Suchman and the state privatisation agency APB's board of directors were sacked in a scandal over irregular payments from the state privatisation agency APV to an advisor.
Kiss said Fazakas would be appointed following his hearing in a committee of the Parliament next week, adding the government would set up APV's new director board next Thursday.
Fazakas was state secretary at the industry and trade ministry until the summer when he was named ambassador to Germany, Hungary's biggest trade partner.
Csiha is a lawyer who is state secretary at the justice ministry.
